target: USWDS confirmation, acknowledgement and forced-action dismissal conditions
observed_behavior: USWDS distinguishes ordinary confirmation dialogs (usually invoked by the user with choices to continue or not) from acknowledgement gates requiring an explicit selection before navigation can proceed. For those forced-action cases, it advises preventing dismissal without choosing, disabling the conventional close affordance, and presenting a clear path to accept or reject; its component documents data-force-action on .usa-modal for that behavior. An example concerns impending session timeout. Elsewhere the same page documents conventional close buttons and data-close-modal, so the forced-action behavior is a deliberately bounded variant, not normal dismissal for all modals.
context: W07 B4 K3 bounded first-party USWDS Modal reference; source sections: Guidance — When to use the modal component; Using the modal component; Modal variants. Explanatory DESIGN_SYSTEM / OFFICIAL_REFERENCE only; not cross-source or runtime evidence.
limitations: An acknowledgement gate is a specific USWDS scenario; forced-action dismissal must not be prescribed universally.
The page's description of disabling closing does not prove the behavior actually occurs in any implementation or demonstrate WCAG compliance.
A time-out notice is an example, not proof that other involuntary interruptions or consent mechanisms are appropriate.
The page documents regular closers and forced action as separate cases; do not flatten their dismissal implications.
No keyboard exit, close/cancel, popup layer, inactivity timer, or user-choice outcome was tested in this Forge lane.
